title: Ekwo country pack, version 1
description: A country is data, not code. This file describes every document of packs/<cc>/: the manifest (the root of this schema), taxes.json, tax_report.json, statements.json, i18n/<lang>.json and the columns of accounts.csv. Nothing here is executable: there is no script field, and there will not be one. What a pack cannot express is a core issue, not a pack extension.

name.description: The country in English, as country_defaults.name holds it.

version.description: Patch: a label, a translation, a source. Minor: an addition, or a validity that closes. Major: a new declaration form or a new statement framework.

schema_min.description: Timestamp of the oldest migration this pack needs.

released_at.description: When this version of the pack was published. Recorded in country_packs.

charts.description: The charts of accounts this country offers. Exactly one is the default. Left out entirely, the pack has one chart called `default` whose accounts are in accounts.csv — which is what a pack written before charts existed says.

box.description: Identifier of a box on a declaration form. Immutable inside a form version.

box_ref.description: A box named in a plus/minus list. Bare, it sums every kind recorded in that box; qualified ("08:tax"), it sums that kind only — the French CA3 carries a base and a tax on the same line, the Belgian boxes do not.

certification.description: Who stands behind this pack. `ekwo init` prints the status, so an operator knows what they installed. A golden test proves internal coherence, never legal truth.

status.description: community: contributed, not read by an accountant. maintained: maintained by Ekwo and not yet read by one either. reviewed: a named professional has read it, and is named in `by`. Writing the pack is not reviewing it, which is why there is no status that means "certified by Ekwo".

by.description: The professional who read the pack. Only on a reviewed pack: maintaining is not reviewing, so it stays empty on a maintained one.

on.description: When they read it. Only on a reviewed pack.

sources.description: The legal texts this pack is built from.

language.description: Language a company of this country is installed in unless it asks for another.

rounding_method.description: How this country rounds a tax amount. half_up is half away from zero, which is what every posting does today. Defaults to half_up.

cash_rounding_unit.description: Smallest coin when it is not the cent: 0.05 in Switzerland. Null, like 0, means the cent is the unit.

closing_style.description: How the year-end close moves the result. retained_earnings: straight into retained earnings (UK, US). result_accounts: into a current-year result account that sits on the balance sheet and waits for the meeting that allocates it (FR 120/129). appropriation_accounts: through an appropriation account that is itself part of the income statement, and from there to retained earnings (BE 693/793 to 140/141). Named after the mechanism, never after a country.

region.description: Province or state a company of this country sits in unless it says otherwise, ISO 3166-2 without the country prefix (QC, BC). Null where a country taxes uniformly, which is every country of phase 0. The declarative rules that turn a region into a suggested tax — tax_rule_templates and suggest_tax() — arrive in phase 1 with the Canadian pack; the column exists now so the migration happens once.

account_roles.description: Which account of accounts.csv plays which role. Every value is a code of this pack's chart; a test refuses one that is not.

retained_earnings_loss.description: Where an accumulated loss sits, where the chart keeps one apart from the profit account (BE 141, FR 119). Null falls back to `retained_earnings`.

current_year_result_profit.description: Account the result of the year lands on when the year is profitable (BE 693, FR 120). Null under `retained_earnings` closing.

current_year_result_loss.description: The same for a loss (BE 793, FR 129). Belgium and France both keep the two apart, so this is a pair and not one account.

journal_roles.description: Which journal of the pack a document falls back to.

opening.description: Journal the opening entry and the year-end entries are booked on. Its type is `opening`.

chart.description: One chart of accounts of a country. A country has one or several; its taxes, its journals and its declaration form are common to them, and its financial statements are per chart when they differ — a Belgian ASBL and a French association keep different books from a company and file the same VAT return.

code.description: Immutable once published. `default` on the chart a country shipped before this list existed.

name.description: What the chart is called where such a name belongs: PCMN, PCG, SKR04.

accounts.description: CSV file of this chart, relative to the pack directory. The default chart keeps accounts.csv.

default.description: Exactly one chart of a pack has it. `ekwo init` installs it when nobody names another.

audience.description: Who keeps books on it — companies, nonprofits, a profession. The core does nothing with it; an installer shows it.

statements.description: Financial statements this chart reports on, by their code in statements.json. A statement named by exactly one chart belongs to that chart; one named by several, or by none, fits every chart of the country.

certification.description: How much this chart in particular has been read, when it differs from the pack as a whole. Left out, the pack's own status stands.

documents.description: What the law of this country says about an invoice. Data only: the renderer prints the mentions, the pack says which and when.

numbering.description: Whether the law forbids a hole in the sequence. The first two compile to numbering_gapless = true; whether the counter restarts each year is readable in number_format, which carries the year or does not.

number_format.description: Pattern of a document number: {CODE} the series, {YYYY} or {YY} the year, {MM} the month, {NNNN} the counter zero-padded to as many N as are written, with literal text between them. Nothing reads it yet — next_entry_number() produces CODE/YYYY/NNNN — and a pack declares what its numbers look like so a numbering engine that consumes a pattern changes no number when it arrives.

legal_payment_days.description: Payment term the law sets in the absence of an agreement. Not a seller's own terms.

late_payment_reference.description: Where the interest rate and the recovery indemnity come from, in one sentence.

tax_point.description: When the tax becomes chargeable under the country's general rule. A tax that departs from it says cash_basis itself, which is how France taxes goods on delivery and services on collection without a second country field.

mentions.description: The sentences the law requires on an invoice, and when each applies.

code.description: Immutable once published. A wording that changes is a valid_to and a new row, never an edit.

applies_when.description: A closed vocabulary, never an expression: a pack that could write a condition would be a pack that executes. Six of the nine are resolved from the treatment of the taxes a document's lines carry; late_payment is about the direction of the document; cash_basis about the tax; small_business about a regime the core does not record, so that one is data a renderer fetches and no view ever selects.

text_i18n.description: The same sentence in other languages, by language code.

sequence.description: Order the mentions are printed in. Defaults to the position in the array, times ten.

legal_reference.description: The article that requires this sentence. A mention without a source cannot be reviewed.

einvoicing.description: The structured invoice this country expects, and the identifiers a party is addressed by on the network.

profile.description: peppol-bis-3, factur-x-en16931, xrechnung, pint-*. Null where electronic invoicing is not a thing.

mandatory_from.description: The day the obligation starts. Where reception and emission start on different days this is reception, which is what binds every company at once; the emission calendar, which usually depends on the size of the company, belongs in the legal reference until the core can hold a size.

party_scheme.description: ISO 6523 ICD of the identifier a party is addressed by, four digits. One value: where a country has several registration identifiers, the pack declares the one its invoices carry and names the others in the legal reference.

vat_scheme.description: ISO 6523 ICD of the VAT identifier, four digits. Distinct from party_scheme: a company is addressed by its registration number and taxed on its VAT number.

bank.description: The file formats a bank of this country delivers and accepts, most usual first. A known list rather than free text, because a parser is written against a format and not against a name somebody typed.

accounts_csv.title: One row of accounts.csv
accounts_csv.description: accounts.csv is a strict CSV subset: a header line `code,parent,type,reconcilable,name,sequence`, one row per account, no newline inside a field, a field quoted only when it holds a comma or a quote, and a quote doubled inside a quoted field. A chart of accounts is flat and long, every tool on the market exchanges it as CSV, and a reviewer reads one line per account in a diff. An empty field is null. Values here are the parsed row.

code.description: Immutable once published, and so is its type: reclassifying a code would reclassify history. Add a code and deprecate the other.

parent.description: Code of the parent account, empty at the top of the chart.

name.description: In the pack's own language. Other languages live in i18n/<lang>.json.

statement_hint.description: Free note: the statement line this account is meant for. Read by nothing today — the rules of a statement decide — and kept so a chart can carry the intent.

code.description: Immutable once published, and so is its meaning. A new rate is a new code plus a valid_to on the old one, never an edit.

kind.description: A label that drives the reports, never the calculation: a GST is computed exactly like a VAT. Defaults to vat.

rate.description: A percentage when amount_type is percent, an amount when it is fixed.

legal_reference.description: The article this rate comes from. A pack without sources cannot be reviewed.

exemption_code.description: VATEX-* reason, when the category asks for one.

price_include.description: The unit price already holds the tax (UK and Australian retail). Compiled to a column; the gross-to-net computation arrives with the country that needs it.

recoverable.description: False when the buyer never gets the tax back: American sales tax, Canadian PST. Where the money lands is said by a tax_on_base posting, not by this flag.

cash_basis.description: The tax falls due when the invoice is paid. Compiled to a column by P0-5; the behaviour arrives with P0-6.

cash_basis_transition_account.description: Code of the account the tax waits on until the invoice is paid. Compiled to a column by P0-5, read by P0-6.

jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166-2 with the country prefix, US-CA, CA-QC, for a tax levied by a state. Null in Europe, and distinct from a party's region, which carries no prefix.

report_code.description: Deferred (P0-3): which declaration the boxes below belong to, when a country files several.

group.description: Reserved for phase 1 (Canada): several taxes on one line. The line keeps a single tax, "QC GST+QST", and posting expands it into its members. Refused by the compiler until the core carries it.

postings.description: What the tax writes on the entry and on the return, per kind of document. A credit note usually repeats the invoice with the side or the box factor flipped.

type.description: base carries no account: it is the line itself. tax carries one. tax_on_base carries none either, and for the same reason — a share of the tax that is not recoverable is a cost, so it lands on the accounts of the lines it taxes (Belgian cars at 50 %, French fuel at 80 %).

factor.description: Percentage of the amount that goes to the ledger — of the base on a base posting, of the tax on the two others. Default 100; -100 flips the side, which is how a self-assessed tax nets to zero.

account.description: Code of the ledger account, from accounts.csv. Only on a tax posting: base and tax_on_base take the account of the document line.

box.description: Box of the periodic return this amount lands in.

box_factor.description: Percentage of the amount reported in the box. Default 100; -100 subtracts from the same line.

report.description: Declaration form this box belongs to. Defaults to the code of tax_report.json — a box number is only unique inside one form, which matters the day a country files two at once (Canada: the federal GST/HST return and the Québec one).

sequence.description: Order inside the kind, and part of the natural key. Defaults to the position in the array, times ten.

tax_report.title: tax_report.json
tax_report.description: Deferred (P0-3): accepted and validated here, compiled when tax_report_templates exists. The boxes of a periodic return and the totals derived from them. No expression language: a plus list, a minus list and a floor at zero cover the Belgian 71/72, the French 16/23/25/28 and the British box 5.

floor_zero.description: A negative total is reported as zero, the other side of the pair carrying it.

hidden.description: An intermediate total the form does not print.

framework.title: packs/generic/pack.json
framework.description: A pack with no country: a framework of financial statements that reports by account type and fits any chart of any country. It carries statements and nothing else — no chart, no tax, no journal — which is why it is not the manifest above.

code.description: IFRS-SME. Names the framework, not a country.

language.description: Language the labels below are written in. A translation goes in i18n/, like any pack.

statements.title: statements.json
statements.description: The financial statements of a pack. An empty list is a valid pack — a country without statements reports on the generic framework by account type, which is what the eighteen account types buy.

taxonomy.description: Taxonomy the `xbrl` fact keys of this statement are written against, as `name:version` — `nbb-cbso:26.0`. The format library that reads those keys carries the table of that very version; a statement whose keys were written against another one resolves them onto the wrong lines, silently. Null where no filing format reads this statement.

xbrl.description: What an XBRL filing writes for this line. The NBB CBSO taxonomy is dimensional, so the value is a fact key — a metric and its dimension members, `met:am1|bas:m2` — not an element name. Null where nothing is verified.

statement_rule.description: How accounts reach a line. Presentation may map by code range — the NBB schema, the liasse and every XBRL taxonomy do — where choosing an account to post to by prefix stays forbidden.

i18n.title: i18n/<lang>.json
i18n.description: Labels in another language, by code. Deferred to P0-2, where account_templates.name_i18n receives them and install_country_template copies the language the company chose. A missing key is not an error: the pack's own label stands.
